title: Introduce region-pin encryption mapper, RBAC v2 residency-assertions, and audit-exception handler
author: Sofia Martinez
description:
Motivation: Customers operating in regulated jurisdictions need stronger guarantees that KMS usage and audit records respect tenant region pins while avoiding noise from benign audit failures. This PR wires a lightweight "residency-enforcer" shim into the request path and introduces an encryption mapper that selects a region-scoped KMS alias before key-wrap, plus an audit-exception handler that classifies and deduplicates expected vs. unexpected audit write errors.

What this changes (summary):
- Add a residency assertion extension to RBAC v2: services can now declare and verify tenant.residency.claims before KMS calls. The verifier supports explicit geozone and soft-affinity modes.
- Introduce kms.EncryptionMapper (small, testable component) that maps service/tenant claims + scope policy -> region-prefixed alias (e.g., alias/redwood/eu-west/tenant-abc) and records a mapping hint in request metadata.
- Add audit/exception handler that: (a) tags audit writes with residency provenance, (b) suppresses duplicate transient audit errors (with configurable window), and (c) surfaces high-severity audit policy violations as SLO alerts.
- Wire residency-enforcer as a middleware in the internal request router (runs before KMS calls and after auth).
- Add config flags to allow conservative rollout: rbacv2.residency.enabled (per-cluster), kms.mapper.mode = [strict|affinity|fallback], audit.handler.dedupe_window_ms.

Why not reuse existing residency middleware? The existing region-pin middleware handled routing but did not participate in RBAC decisions or provide KMS alias mapping; this PR complements it by making KMS choice policy-aware and making audit behavior deterministic during transient KMS errors.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc: linear ENG-3411 (link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3411/residency-enforcer-kms-mapper)
- [x] Unit tests for EncryptionMapper and ResidencyVerifier (new test package)
- [x] Integration test that replays tenant request with conflicting region claim (eu vs us) and verifies mapper picks KMS alias per policy
- [x] E2E scenario on staging (manual): simulated KMS throttling + audit sink flaps, validated dedupe and SLO alerting
- [x] Console flag added for controlled rollout

Compatibility and rollout plan: Start with kms.mapper.mode=affinity in staging for two weeks, enable RBAC residency checks in shadow mode (log-only) for 48 hours, then flip to enforced for clients that have opted in. If audit dedupe suppresses true positives, the dedupe window can be lowered; default set conservatively to 1000ms.

Security considerations: The ResidencyVerifier adds decision telemetry but does not persist keys or sensitive contexts; KMS alias selection happens server-side only. A secondary audit step records the alias hint but redacts tenant identifiers in exported telemetry.

Notes on tests and observability: 
- Added per-request telemetry tags: residency.reason, kms.alias.hint, audit.suppressed=true/false.
- New dashboard tile (Console) tracking "Residency enforcement rejections" and "Audit dedupe rate".

Files changed (high-level): added residency verifier and mapper packages, small changes in request router, new unit/integration tests, console feature flag wiring, and dashboards.

References: design doc + linear ENG-3411, related work ENG-2971 (geo-routing refactor).
release_notes: Adds RBAC v2 residency assertions, a KMS alias mapping component to enforce region-pin behavior, and an audit-exception deduper to reduce noisy alerts during transient KMS failures. Rollout gated behind cluster feature flags.
commit_summary: feat(kms): implement EncryptionMapper and alias resolution logic
chore(router): wire residency-enforcer middleware into request pipeline
feat(audit): audit-exception handler with dedupe window and severity mapping
docs: add rollout notes and console flag help text
test(integration): add conflicting-claim and kinesis-audit-flap tests
review_thread: Maya Patel: Nice design. Two main asks: ensure the mapper can't be spoofed by crafted headers and add a unit test for the redaction path when telemetry export is enabled.
Sofia Martinez: Addressed — mapper now validates tenant claim against the auth token signature and we added telemetry redaction unit tests (verifier_test.go).
Owen Li: Found a race in the dedupe window counter during heavy parallel writes — suggested use of an atomic slab.
author_responses: Sofia Martinez: Switched to a sharded atomic counter (audit/exception_handler.go). Added comment and bench for worst-case concurrency.
Sofia Martinez: Also added console feature flag for emergency kill-switch as requested by platform ops.
notes: Staging run showed 0.7% increase in average KMS call path latency due to additional metadata lookup; acceptable within SLOs. Observability tags were reviewed and accepted by security.
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (flaky on first run, retried)

deploy_instructions: Enable rbacv2.residency.enabled=false in production cluster initially. Set kms.mapper.mode=affinity. After 48h of shadow logging, enable rbacv2.residency.enabled=true for opted-in tenants via console. Monitor residency_enforcement_rejections_total and audit_dedupe_events_total for anomalies.
